    NoonTalk needs continued financial support from CEO Dasmond Koh, auditors warn

    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 6:09
    Instaread
    2,835
    PublishedOct 15, 2026, 05:26am
    Read AI summary on Stomp Bites

    Kang Wan Chern
    The Straits Times
    Oct 14, 2026

    NoonTalk Media’s financial difficulties appear to remain unsolved despite financial support from its chief executive and controlling shareholder Dasmond Koh.

    Auditors flagged significant uncertainty over the talent management, multimedia production and events firm’s ability to continue operating, citing its losses, cash outflows and liabilities exceeding assets.

    The warning was disclosed in an Oct 14 announcement on its audited financial statements for the year ended June 30.

    Koh has given a written undertaking to provide the necessary financial support for 12 months from Oct 14 to help the company meet its debts as they fall due, NoonTalk said in the statement.

    The support will come mainly from Koh’s holdings of Singapore-listed shares, which can be converted into cash when the company calls upon him. It follows Koh’s conversion of a $1.8 million loan to NoonTalk into company shares in July.

    This comes as the auditing team highlighted several factors that could cast significant doubt on NoonTalk’s ability to continue operating.

    The group reported a loss of $2.55 million for the financial year ended June 30, and used $2.16 million in cash in its operations.

    Poll Form!

    How has the haze affected you?

    At the end of June, its total liabilities exceeded its assets by $2.93 million. Its short-term liabilities also exceeded its short-term assets by about $2.93 million.

    Short-term liabilities are obligations due within a year, while short-term assets include cash and other assets expected to be converted into cash or used within that period.

    The auditors added that the assumption that NoonTalk could continue operating depended on continued financial support from Koh.

    Besides Koh’s support, NoonTalk said it expected income from a new platform marketing business in China. Its subsidiary Ruiqi Zhongxin (Chengdu) Culture Technology has entered into a framework agreement with a third party to carry out promotional campaigns and place advertisements on ByteDance’s Ocean Qianchuan platform.

    The board said its cash flow forecast, which took account of potential income from the marketing services, and planned cost reductions, indicated that the group could generate positive operating cash flows.

    NoonTalk is also evaluating options to raise or obtain additional funds for its day-to-day operations.

    For now, the board said sufficient information had been disclosed for trading in NoonTalk’s shares to continue in an orderly manner.

    The Catalist-listed company will also continue reporting its financial results quarterly instead of twice a year because of the material uncertainty over its ability to continue operating.

    Bonding over Singlish: Carrie Wong taught co-star Lee Joon-gi different ways to use ‘lah’

    1,705
    2
    PublishedOct 10, 2026, 11:06pm
    |
    UpdatedOct 10, 2026, 11:18pm
    Read AI summary on Stomp Bites

    Benson Ang
    The Straits Times
    Oct 9, 2026

    Local actress Carrie Wong was unfazed about being Singapore’s sole representative in Kidnap Game, her first big-scale international production, saying it gave her the drive to excel instead.

    The pan-Asian drama brings together stars from seven Asian markets for a high-stakes suspense thriller.

    The cast includes Japan’s Kentaro Sakaguchi, South Korea’s Lee Joon-gi, Taiwan’s Alice Ko, Hong Kong’s Stanley Yau, the Philippines’ Joel Torre and Thailand’s Praew Narupornkamol Chaisang, who attended the world premiere of Kidnap Game in Tokyo on Oct 2.

    Filmed across Hong Kong, Taipei, Seoul, Tokyo, Singapore, Bangkok, Manila and Okinawa, the 11-episode series is available on Viu, with new episodes available on Tuesdays at 9pm.

    Wong, 32, told The Straits Times in an online interview: “When you feel pressure, (it means) what you are doing genuinely matters to you, and that makes me just want to work harder and give more of myself.

    “I don’t let this pressure overwhelm me. I just focus on doing my best and making the most out of this entire opportunity.”

    Wong plays Janice, a flight attendant whose boyfriend gets abducted in Singapore, in one of seven kidnappings that happen simultaneously in different cities. She then receives a message telling her that she has to play a “kidnap game” and complete a mission before the others to save her loved one.

    “Janice is a very happy-go-lucky girl, the sort who is naturally funny and does not care about many things in the world. The only thing she wants is to marry her (boyfriend).”

    Wong said Kidnap Game’s main director was keen to cast her after seeing her performance in local action drama Shero (2023).

    All her scenes were filmed in Singapore, in places such as Joo Chiat and Merlion Park, around November 2025.

    Poll Form!

    How has the haze affected you?

    Lee, who plays a retired surgeon whose daughter is kidnapped in Seoul, was the only other main cast member Wong worked alongside.

    The actress joked: “In a survival game, some characters tend to find teammates.”

    Off-screen, Wong found the 44-year-old star of historical film The King And The Clown (2005) and romantic comedy series My Girl (2005 to 2006) to be humble and funny.

    She said: “He is so open to listening to others, and I did not feel any pressure on set with him. For someone who has been in the industry for so long, it is amazing to have such a quality.

    “And he looks very, very young, like he has not aged in 20 years.”

    The K-actor was curious about Singlish and asked Wong to explain to him how the word “lah” has different meanings in different contexts, such as “eat lah” and “cannot lah”, she recalled. “He is just a funny, extroverted person.”

    Kidnap Game also gave Wong the opportunity to play a flight attendant, an occupation she had considered before going into acting in 2014.

    She said that when she was 17 and studying hospitality and tourism management at Nanyang Polytechnic, the possibility of interning at an airline came up. She eventually chose to intern at another company instead.

    She said: “After I got older, my friends and I agreed being a flight attendant would not have suited me. I am too hard-headed.”

    Unfortunately, none of her scenes take place on an aircraft. “After the kidnapping starts, there are more important matters.”

    That said, she loved the uniform she got to wear for the show, calling it “super pretty”.

    • Kidnap Game is available on Viu.
